text: Pecorino is deliberately made attractive to the cheese fly: it is lightly pressed, briefly brined and its rind pierced and oiled, so that Piophila casei lays its eggs inside. The larvae break down the paste, which turns soft to spreadably creamy with a strong, penetrating, piquant taste.

steps.note: Short, so the salt does not deter the fly.
Holes with a drop of oil, so the fly lays its eggs inside.
The larvae break the paste down, with few turnings, from late spring to autumn.
